title: Casebook — Carrying the Paid Deposit Percentage into a Made-to-Order Remake (Pre-Orders & Back-Orders)
content:
**Governing rule.** The remake deposit percentage of a Pre-Orders & Back-Orders Made-to-Order remake carries the percentage paid on the cancelled pair. That percentage is the pair's deposit charged times 100, divided by its reserved unit price times its units, rounded half up to two decimal places. How much is carried depends on how soon after the customer asked to cancel the pair the remake is taken:

| Remake taken | Remake deposit percentage |
|---|---|
| Within 14 days of the date the customer asked to cancel the pair | The paid percentage |
| From 15 days up to 45 days | The average of the paid percentage and the Made-to-Order Reservation deposit percentage (50) |
| More than 45 days | The Made-to-Order Reservation deposit percentage (50) |

The date the customer asked to cancel is the date of the most recent cancellation request on the pair. Days are calendar days from that date to the day the remake is taken. The deposit charged is the deposit charge entry on the pair's history. The average is used as it stands, with no rounding of its own.

**Cases.** All cases are hypothetical. The pair was reserved at $400.00 for one unit, with a deposit charged of $120.00, so the paid percentage is 30.00.

| Case | Days since the customer asked | Remake deposit percentage |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 10 | 30.00 |
| 2 | 14 | 30.00 |
| 3 | 15 | 40 (the average of 30.00 and 50) |
| 4 | 45 | 40 |
| 5 | 46 | 50 |

**Rounding of the paid percentage (hypothetical).** A pair reserved at $455.00 with a deposit charged of $150.00 has a paid percentage of 150 times 100, divided by 455, which is 32.967. Rounded half up to two places, that gives 32.97. Taken 20 days after the customer asked, the remake carries the average of 32.97 and 50, which is 41.485.
